== Verify Group Ownership of Message of the Day Banner
----
To check the group ownership of /etc/motd,
run the command:
$ ls -lL /etc/motd
If properly configured, the output should indicate the following group-owner:

  root
  
      Is it the case that /etc/motd does not have a group owner of
root
?
----

== Verify ownership of Message of the Day Banner
----
To check the ownership of /etc/motd,
run the command:
$ ls -lL /etc/motd
If properly configured, the output should indicate the following owner:
root
      Is it the case that /etc/motd does not have an owner of root?
----

== Verify permissions on Message of the Day Banner
----
To check the permissions of /etc/motd,
run the command:
$ ls -l /etc/motd
If properly configured, the output should indicate the following permissions:
-rw-r--r--
      Is it the case that /etc/motd does not have unix mode -rw-r--r--?
----

discussion:
## Verify Group Ownership of Message of the Day Banner

To properly set the group owner of `/etc/motd`, run the command:

  
```
$ sudo chgrp root /etc/motd
```

**Rationale:**

Display of a standardized and approved use notification before granting
access to the operating system ensures privacy and security notification
verbiage used is consistent with applicable federal laws, Executive Orders,
directives, policies, regulations, standards, and guidance.

Proper group ownership will ensure that only root user can modify the banner.

## Verify ownership of Message of the Day Banner

To properly set the owner of `/etc/motd`, run the command:

  
```
$ sudo chown root /etc/motd 
```

**Rationale:**

Display of a standardized and approved use notification before granting
access to the operating system ensures privacy and security notification
verbiage used is consistent with applicable federal laws, Executive Orders,
directives, policies, regulations, standards, and guidance.

Proper ownership will ensure that only root user can modify the banner.

## Verify permissions on Message of the Day Banner

To properly set the permissions of `/etc/motd`, run the command:

```
$ sudo chmod 0644 /etc/motd
```

**Rationale:**

Display of a standardized and approved use notification before granting
access to the operating system ensures privacy and security notification
verbiage used is consistent with applicable federal laws, Executive Orders,
directives, policies, regulations, standards, and guidance.

Proper permissions will ensure that only root user can modify the banner.

steps.name: Verify Group Ownership of Message of the Day Banner
steps.shell:
newgroup=""
if getent group "0" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  newgroup="0"
fi

if [[ -z "${newgroup}" ]]; then
  >&2 echo "0 is not a defined group on the system"
else
if ! stat -c "%g %G" "/etc/motd" | grep -E -w -q "0"; then
    chgrp --no-dereference "$newgroup" /etc/motd
fi

fi

steps.name: Verify ownership of Message of the Day Banner
steps.shell:
newown=""
if id "0" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  newown="0"
fi

if [[ -z "$newown" ]]; then
  >&2 echo "0 is not a defined user on the system"
else
if ! stat -c "%u %U" "/etc/motd" | grep -E -w -q "0"; then
    chown --no-dereference "$newown" /etc/motd
fi

fi
